## Calculation and selective reporting

Calculate complete and recruitment targets using the same structured object.

```{r}
library(aiimsulator)
x <- ss_proportion(.50, .05, nonresponse = .10)
x
ss_table(x)
```

Get the general equation, substitution and report separately:

```{r}
ss_equation(x, "formula", "text")
ss_equation(x, "substituted_values", "text")
ss_report(x, formula = FALSE, substituted_values = FALSE,
          results = TRUE, assumptions = TRUE, format = "text")
```

## Additional methods

```{r}
ss_mean(sd = 12, precision = 3)
ss_two_means(difference = 5, pooled_sd = 12)
ss_two_proportions(.20, .35)
ss_yamane(1500)
ss_diagnostic(objective = "joint", sensitivity = .85,
              specificity = .9, recruitment = "separate")
ss_correlation(r = .3)
ss_auc(auc = .80, precision = .05)
```

## Study-design qualifications

Do not use this package to justify clinically meaningful margins or effect
sizes without external scientific evidence. Normal, Fisher-z and Hanley-McNeil
planning approximations have design limitations. A cluster-randomized trial
cannot generally be planned correctly by simple multiplication of an independent
individual sample size by a design effect. The accompanying documentation
records these boundaries.
